title: Etiquette & language
body:
Gion's private alleys (around Kosode Koji, on the west side of Hanamikoji) have been off-limits to tourists since May 2024, with a ¥10,000 fine posted for entering or photographing on them — a response to tourists chasing and touching geiko/maiko. The main public streets, Hanamikoji itself and Yasaka Shrine, stay open as normal.

Nishiki Market's own trade association asks visitors not to eat while walking through the arcade — buy, then eat in front of or inside the shop you bought from, not on the move. It's a posted request, not a fined law, but it's worth following in a market that's already crowded.

A slight bow works for most everyday interactions (thanking a shopkeeper, apologizing for a bump); a spoken "sumimasen" (excuse me / sorry) covers getting someone's attention. Remove shoes wherever a raised floor or tatami room signals it, kaiseki restaurants included.
